reason: The hypothesis combines the known effect of interstitial carbon on strength and ductility in TWIP-TRIP HEAs (P20) with the known effect of grain boundary serration/precipitate pinning on high-temperature creep (P2, P3, P5) and applies this combination to room-temperature creep and corrosion in the Cantor alloy, a regime and property combination not directly studied in any single passage. The link between carbide pinning and simultaneous room-temperature creep and corrosion improvement is a synthesis of separate findings.
